channel.title: The Catholic Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Catholic Review (catholicreview.org)

item.title: Notre Dame Prep develops new commons area
item.description: The $10 million project will transform the 1960s-style cafeteria into a state-of-the-art commons center featuring flexible seating areas, a student cafe and a brand-new kitchen with a wood-fired pizza oven.

item.title: Pope Leo appoints Vincentian sister as new deputy of Vatican press office
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has appointed Croatian Vincentian Sister Nina Benedikta Krapic as the deputy director of the Holy See Press Office.

item.title: Catechist, pregnant wife among kidnapped in latest anti-Christian attacks in Nigeria
item.description: Several gunmen abducted 32 people in Nigeria's Kaduna state, including a catechist and his pregnant wife, in an attack that has increased fears of Christians in the country who have been targeted over several weeks.

item.title: Ave Maria University battles measles outbreak
item.description: A Catholic university in Florida is battling an outbreak of measles among its students, with 7 in quarantine as of Feb. 11.

item.title: Movie Review: ‘Crime 101’
item.description: All three of the main characters in "Crime 101" (Amazon MGM), the film adaptation of Don Winslow's 2020 novella, are dealing with lives and careers that have slammed into a wall.

item.title: Head of Ukrainian Catholic Church meets with Pope Leo, calls Ukraine ‘wounded but alive’
item.description: Major Archbishop Sviatoslav Shevchuk spoke with Pope Leo at the Apostolic Palace Feb. 12, the second personal audience the prelate has had since meeting with the pope days after his election, said the UGCC press office in an update released shortly after the meeting.

item.title: How Archbishop Sheen embodied the 7 key virtues
item.description: With his beatification once again on track, Archbishop Fulton J. Sheen will be memorialized in the Church for reasons far beyond his contributions to the Church’s intellectual life or his evangelical zeal, incredible and legendary though they are.

item.title: A quick history of Mardi Gras
item.description: In times of greater Lenten austerity in Catholic countries, Mardi Gras offered an opportunity for households to consume some foods they would not enjoy until Easter.

item.title: Oldest priest in Archdiocese of Newark reflects on 104 years of life and 78 years of ministry
item.description: At age 104, Msgr. James C. Turro is the oldest priest in the Archdiocese of Newark -- and possibly the United States -- and also holds the distinction of being the oldest living alumnus of Seton Hall University.

item.title: 6 Catholic athletes from past Winter Olympics inspire with stories of faith, endurance
item.description: The Catholic athletes at the Games this year are joining a long tradition of Catholic Olympians who have made history with their inspiring stories of faith and endurance. Here are just some of the Catholic stories that came out of past Winter Games.
